{{Quote|As you grow older, you'll find that you occasionally have to deal with an excess of testosterone. Often on minor worlds like Ansion. I dislike such distractions.|Luminara Unduli, to Barriss Offee, after the Jedi Master repelled a group of amorous men|<ref name="TAS">''[[The Approaching Storm]]''</ref>}}
'''Testosterone''' was something strongly associated with behaviors exhibited by [[Gender/Legends|males]],<ref name="TAS" /> including [[Human/Legends|Human]] men.<ref name="TZERO">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> This correlation was directly related to actions that were lustful,<ref name="TAS" /> aggressive,<ref name="TZERO" /> or boastful.<ref name="Taster's Choice: The Tale of Jabba's Chef">{{StoryCite|story=Taster's Choice: The Tale of Jabba's Chef|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|You know, the Rebellion may be led by a robed ex-Senator and a Princess without a homeworld, but for all that girl power on top, the rank-and-file pilots have been decidedly testosterone-heavy. Miss Neth brings a little gender equity to the game (and Rogue Squadron) and serves as a back-up pilot for Gray Squadron 2.|[[Cory J. Herndon]], on [[Karie Neth/Legends|Karie Neth]]|<ref name="DP">{{GamerCite|2|Deck Plans}}</ref>}}
Testosterone was first mentioned in a short story written by [[Barbara Hambly]] that was featured in a collection called ''[[Tales from Jabba's Palace]]'', ''[[Taster's Choice: The Tale of Jabba's Chef]]''. It has since been referenced in novels written by [[Karen Traviss]] and [[Alan Dean Foster]], as well as some of [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|Living Force]] supplements.

In real life, testosterone is a hormone that men and, to a significantly lesser extent, women produce in their endocrine systems. In men, it increases muscle, maintains energy, fuels a sexual drive, and increases aggression, so it has come to be associated with behaviors related to these developments and males in general.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.webmd.com/men/features/keep-testosterone-in-balance|text=Keep Testosterone in Balance|author=Tony Rehagen|work=[[Wikipedia:WebMD|WebMD]]|archivedate=20260223183345}}</ref>
